Requirement: Estimates are built from items, routings and rates, revised with numbered versions, and an accepted estimate becomes the order without retyping.
What the vendor must show: Revise an estimate twice, then convert the accepted version into an order.

Requirement: Each order shows its status (in production, shipped, invoiced, paid) to sales without asking accounting.
What the vendor must show: Open one order as a salesperson and show its status and every document on it.

Requirement: Customer-specific prices and discounts are held on the customer and applied on the order automatically.
What the vendor must show: Enter an order for a customer with a contract price and show the price applied.

Requirement: Purchase requests from production or stores become purchase orders after approval, with the approver and date kept.
What the vendor must show: Raise a request, approve it as a manager, and show the purchase order and its approval record.

Requirement: Vendor bills are matched to the purchase order and the receipt (three-way match) before they are approved for payment.
What the vendor must show: Post a bill with a quantity higher than received and show that it is held.

Requirement: Open purchase orders and late deliveries are listed by vendor and promised date.
What the vendor must show: Show the purchase orders past their promised date this week.

Requirement: Stock is held by location and bin, in raw, in-progress and finished states.
What the vendor must show: Show one item's stock by location, and what is issued to open jobs.

Requirement: Material can be reserved for a job or order, and reserved stock is not available to others.
What the vendor must show: Reserve the last units for one order and try to issue them to another.

Requirement: Lot or serial numbers are captured at receiving and shipping, with a trace from supplier to customer.
What the vendor must show: Trace one lot to the customers who received it.

Requirement: Cycle counts run by ABC class with blind counts and a reason on every adjustment.
What the vendor must show: Run a blind count on one bin and post a difference with its reason.

Requirement: Stock is valued by the method your accountant chose (FIFO, average or standard) and posted to the books.
What the vendor must show: Show the stock value report and the matching ledger balance.

Requirement: Jobs carry routings with operations, machines and planned hours, scheduled against machine capacity.
What the vendor must show: Add a rush job and show which jobs move and which go late.

Requirement: Labor and machine time are recorded per operation from the floor, by scan or tablet.
What the vendor must show: Clock one operator onto an operation and off again, and show the hours on the job.

Requirement: Scrap and rework are recorded against the job and operation, with a reason.
What the vendor must show: Record scrap on one operation and show it in the job cost.

Requirement: Job cost (material, labor, outside processing, overhead) is compared with the estimate while the job is open.
What the vendor must show: Show estimated against actual cost for a job in progress.

Requirement: Only complete, inspected work can be shipped; partial shipments are tracked against the order.
What the vendor must show: Ship part of an order and show what remains open.

Requirement: Packing lists, labels and bills of lading print from the order with the carrier and tracking number kept.
What the vendor must show: Ship one order and show its documents and tracking number.

Requirement: Invoices, bills, payments and stock value post to QuickBooks or the ledger once, with failures shown to a person.
What the vendor must show: Make a post fail (for example a closed period) and show where the failure appears.

Requirement: Which system owns customers, items, invoices and payments is written down and enforced.
What the vendor must show: Edit a customer in QuickBooks and show what happens in the system.

Requirement: Tax on each invoice line comes from the ship-to address and the item's tax code, from a rate service.
What the vendor must show: Invoice a ship-to address in a city with a district tax and show the jurisdictions.

Requirement: Customers' resale and exemption certificates are held by state with dates, and orders to a state without one are taxed.
What the vendor must show: Ship to a state where the customer has no certificate on file.

Requirement: Sales and order counts by ship-to state for any 12 months, with resale, exempt and taxable sales apart.
What the vendor must show: Run the report for the last 12 months.

Requirement: Each person sees only their role's screens and data; money is hidden from those who don't need it.
What the vendor must show: Sign in as a shop-floor user and show that prices and costs are hidden.

Requirement: Every change to a transaction keeps who, when and the old and new values, and the log can't be switched off.
What the vendor must show: Change an approved order and show the change log.

Requirement: Owners see late jobs, short stock, open orders and cash owed on one screen, from the same records.
What the vendor must show: Show the screen and open one figure to the records behind it.

Requirement: Your data can be exported in full (CSV or database) at any time, without the vendor's help.
What the vendor must show: Export all open orders and the item list now, in the demo.

Requirement: The contract says who owns the code or licence, what happens if you stop paying, and how you get your data out.
What the vendor must show: Ask for the contract clauses in writing before the demo ends.

Requirement: Spreadsheets and the old system are imported and checked row by row; rows that don't match are held for a person.
What the vendor must show: Ask how many of your rows would be imported, how many held, and how a held row is resolved.
